unresolved_added: The model is called feasible because outputs look consistent with expected autonomous-vehicle properties; independent calibration is absent.
Four-meter cells, one-second steps, identical vehicles and class-homogeneous behavior need discretization sensitivity.
Peak and nonpeak arrivals remain independent Poisson processes without overdispersion, serial dependence or entry blocking checks.
The 20 m/s initial speed is asserted harmless without warm-up removal or initial-condition sensitivity.
Safe distance T_r v omits braking distance, leader deceleration, road condition and vehicle class.
Human acceleration/deceleration probabilities are hand-selected without driver-data calibration.
The assumptions say self-driving has no response delay, while simulation uses T_rs=1 second.
Alpha, beta and gamma combine different physical dimensions and are set to one without scaling or stability analysis.
Acceleration lacks explicit physical bounds, jerk limits and a collision-proof invariant; update order is incomplete.
Communication is perfect and instantaneous until a later generic error test; latency and packet loss are absent.
Lane changes omit simultaneous conflicts, reservations, mandatory exits, route incentives and destination response.
P_c=0.5 is uncalibrated, and limited one-factor sensitivity does not validate the lane model.
The interchange uses one cloverleaf, 50-percent movement probabilities and T_inter=10 seconds without data.
A single 24-hour simulation per setting has no seed, replicate count, warm-up, Monte Carlo error or confidence interval.
Average passing time and vehicles present are called capacity although throughput and demand served are not reported.
Cars per second per kilometer mixes temporal flow and spatial density semantics.
Daily counts are divided evenly by direction without a directional data check.
The 224 segments appear equally averaged within roads; length-, volume- and direction-weighted alternatives are absent.
Visual equilibrium locations vary across Summary, Introduction, whole-day velocity, peak velocity and density.
The Summary says velocity doubles from 10 to 50 percent without binding the claim to a specific road/window denominator.
The 70-percent dedicated-lane divider comes from a sparse 30/50/70 grid and one five-lane setup.
Dedicated lanes becoming necessary is stronger than the small simulated gain and ignores cost, compliance, equity and induced demand.
One-factor P_c and a few alpha/beta/gamma combinations do not prove robustness or expose interactions.
The plus/minus one, ten-percent error process is not calibrated to observed failure types or rates, and total probability is ambiguous.
The official letter says communication can eliminate collisions, exceeding simulation evidence.
Reference 6 concerns orbital debris removal and appears unrelated to traffic cellular automata.
No code, raw output, seed policy, exact scheduler, collision assertions or runtime environment is released.
No dedicated strengths/limitations section exists; audit limitations must not be attributed to author self-critique.
